claims.claim: Michigan has no numeric THC limit like the 0.08 alcohol limit; instead it bans driving while under the influence, and a separate zero-tolerance law bars driving with any amount of a Schedule 1 drug, a list that includes marijuana.
claims.details: MCL 257.625(8) (zero tolerance for any amount of a Schedule 1 substance; marihuana is listed in MCL 333.7212(1)(c)). First offense: misdemeanor, up to 93 days, $100 to $500 fine and/or up to 360 hours of community service; six points; mandatory 180-day license suspension (restricted license possible after 30 days). Registered medical patients: the MMMA overrides the zero-tolerance rule, so a patient with THC in their system is liable only if actually under the influence (People v Koon, 494 Mich 1 (2013)). Under 21: the MRTMA does not shield drivers under 21 from MCL 257.625(8) (People v Perry, 338 Mich App 363 (2021)). Adults 21+ who are not patients: the Traffic Benchbook says it is unclear whether violations of the MRTMA's limited conduct will be pursued under the Vehicle Code, and equally unclear whether the Koon holding will be extended to the MRTMA.

MCL 333.27965(4): more than twice the allowed amount is a misdemeanor without jail unless habitual, willful and commercial, or violent. MCL 333.27965(1): conduct within the limits but not authorized (other than driving, school or prison grounds and similar listed conduct) is a civil infraction up to $100 plus forfeiture.
